claims.text: On 2026-10-29 Alexander Koch, CEO of San Francisco's Tau Robotics, announced that customers can now book the company's humanoid cleaners on a recurring subscription, for up to three hours per cleaning, with a 4× sped-up "first take, uncut" video.
It sells "two humanoids, every visit", and for a one-hour visit quotes $60 per visit weekly, $80 every two weeks, $90 every four weeks, and $100 one-time
Tau's Service Terms, last updated 2026-10-24, state the standard fee as "$50 per humanoid per hour" and normally send two humanoids, so $100, $200 or $300 for one, two or three hours.
The Service Terms describe a full charge at booking and contain no recurring-billing clause,
press coverage at the 2026-07-28 launch reported an invite-only service at $30 per hour,
Hoodline's launch write-up described one humanoid per appointment.
it has said it wants about 1,000 cleanings a week in San Francisco by 2027
"The robot is not autonomous. A person is controlling it." and "Every cleaning is recorded. Your operator watches live."
Koch told The Register that each humanoid is jointly controlled by a human operator and AI, that "the balance varies by task"
Tau's own site adds that a supervisor travels with the robots and can take manual control, and that children needing supervision require an adult to be present.
In a CBS interview Koch said the robots will first be trained to imitate human performance and then to exceed it, and that technicians would be phased out around 2028–29.
a MarketWatch-derived summary puts the fleet at about eight robots with roughly 160 paid robot-hours across nearly 100 cleanings
The booking page, however, leaves bathrooms and bedrooms off-limits by default unless the customer asks for them.
Press and trade coverage identify it as a visibly modified Unitree G1;
CBS quotes Koch saying the robots cost $50,000 each to make and that "the camera system, the networking and the computers are all our own".
Bloomberg Línea, relaying the same interview, reports a claimed payback of under a year at 40 hours a week;
MarketWatch coverage summarised by humanoid.guide gives a slightly higher hardware figure of about $55,000 per unit.
Unitree's own spec page lists the G1 at about 1.32 m tall and about 35 kg, 23 degrees of freedom in the base version, an arm payload of about 2 kg
The list price was $16,000 at the May 2024 launch,
A reseller lists the pack at 46.8 V nominal and 421.2 Wh,
The BLS Occupational Employment survey shows the national median for maids and housekeeping cleaners (SOC 37-2012) at $16.08 an hour in May 2023, with 836,230 jobs;
a wage aggregator mirroring the May 2025 data reports a $17.07 median and 860,670 jobs.
IBISWorld sizes US residential cleaning at about $18.8 billion in 2024 and describes a fragmented industry.
A third-party aggregator puts the San Francisco-area mean around $25 an hour, but that is a search-derived figure and I treat it as indicative only.
the often-cited Manila convenience-store operators earn roughly $250–$315 a month but supervise up to 50 robots on a far simpler shelf-stocking task.

On 2026-07-28 the FCC added "foreign-produced advanced robotic devices", including humanoids and quadrupeds, to its Covered List, with exceptions for devices granted a Conditional Approval by the Department of War (Public Notice DA 26-786).
Unitree authorised several products, including the R1, H2 and A2, in the weeks before the rule; the same source puts the US at 13.3% of Unitree's 2025 revenue.
A 2025 arXiv assessment of the platform found persistent telemetry connections to external servers that transmit robot state and sensor data, and static encryption keys in the configuration;

IEEE Spectrum covered "UniPwn", a Bluetooth Low Energy flaw affecting the Go2, B2, G1 and H1 that allowed root takeover through command injection and hardcoded keys (CVE-2025-35027 and CVE-2025-60250);
The Service Privacy Policy says the robot's head and wrist cameras record continuously, faces are not blurred, microphones are disabled, no facial recognition is used,
The company's separate website terms and privacy policy exclude the in-home service and point to these documents, and use a different dispute mechanism.
A summary of the ISO catalogue describes ISO 25785-1 as a draft for dynamically stable industrial mobile robots that explicitly leaves non-industrial settings to ISO 13482,
California's all-party-consent wiretap statute carries $5,000 per violation, which makes Tau's recorded-visit disclosure its main defence;

Mobile ALOHA found that co-training with static-arm data raised whole-task success on tasks such as wiping wine from 50% to 95% and rinsing a pan from 0% to 80%, using about 50 demonstrations per task mixed with an 825-episode static pool.

The pi*0.6 work reports that on-robot reinforcement learning with expert interventions more than doubled throughput and roughly halved failures on the hardest tasks, with each box-assembly iteration mixing 600 autonomous trials and 360 with expert interventions.
the HIW-500 dataset offers over 500 hours of G1 whole-body teleoperation across 12 real homes under a CC BY 4.0 licence,
a delivery tracker found no confirmed customer receipts as of late October 2026 against a stated 2026 shipping window.
Sunday Robotics raised $165 million at a $1.15 billion valuation in March 2026 and targets a household beta later this year.
Reported funding is $2.6 million pre-seed from one outlet, with no named investors in any fetched source and a second estimate of $3 million;
